question: The amount payable on maturity of a certain sum invested at a certain rate of simple interest per annum for one year was ₹1,484. If the rate of interest had been 2% higher, the amount would have been ₹26.50 more. What was the interest that was paid on the sum invested at the original rate?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Principal = 100%

 As per question,

2% = 26.50

Principal = 100% = (26.50/2) × 100 = 1325

Interest = Amount - Principal = 1484 - 1325 = 159

∴ The interest that was paid on the sum invested at the original rate is ₹159.

Given:

The amount payable on maturity of a certain sum invested at a certain rate of simple interest per annum for one year was ₹1,484.

If the rate of interest had been 2% higher, the amount would have been ₹26.50 more.
